title: Order API timeouts overnight
executive_summary: INC-004: Order API timeouts from 02:15Z were caused by order-service exhausting CPU and heap, which triggered long GC pauses and worker-thread saturation. Upstream dependencies and request volume were flat, and no deploys or config changes were recorded. The trigger of the resource growth is still unknown; it needs host/process-level verification.

hypotheses.description: Resource saturation inside order-service (CPU and heap pressure from a co-located batch job or a memory leak) causing GC thrashing and worker-pool exhaustion. Mechanism: Memory climbs from ~02:10, GC pauses start at 02:08 (up to 9.7s), CPU reaches ~100%, the order-worker pool saturates (active=200, queue ~19k), and requests exceed the 5s deadline, producing timeouts and errors.

root_cause_statement: MOST PROBABLE EXPLANATION (INFERENCE, not confirmed): resource_saturation in order-service - Resource saturation inside order-service (CPU and heap pressure from a co-located batch job or a memory leak) causing GC thrashing and worker-pool exhaustion.
corrective_actions: Immediately restart or drain order-service instances showing GC thrashing and saturated worker pools, or scale out to restore capacity.
Identify and stop/throttle any batch or background process running on order-service nodes from ~02:00Z.
Shed or bound the order-worker queue so it cannot grow to ~19k, with fast-fail on overload.
preventive_actions: Isolate batch/reconciliation workloads from serving nodes (see hist-HIST-2025-040).
Set heap and GC alerting thresholds, and cap the worker queue size.
Add memory-growth leak detection for order-service.
monitoring_recommendations: Alert on GC pause >1s and on order-worker queue depth >100.
Alert on order-service CPU >85% for 5 min and memory >75%.
Track the order-service timeout rate and p95 against the 200ms baseline.
limitations: Historical analogy HIST-2025-040 (batch job) is a similarity match only, not confirmation.
Metrics are sampled at 5-minute resolution, so the exact trigger ordering within 02:00-02:15 is uncertain.
[agent-reported gap] No process-level heap, GC, or thread dump data.

Confidence values are rule-based evidence-strength scores, not calibrated probabilities.
conclusion: order-service became resource-saturated on the JVM/host level starting ~02:08Z: CPU rose to ~100% and memory climbed from ~55% to ~80%, with G1 pauses of 2.6–9.7s. Thread pool order-worker saturated (active=200, queue up to ~19k), causing requests to exceed the 5000ms deadline and timeouts to rise from 0.1% to ~6%. Upstream payment-service and postgres-related signals are flat, no deployments or config changes occurred, and the cause of the memory/CPU growth is not yet identified. The most likely explanation is a local resource-saturation event inside order-service (possibly an unscheduled batch/background job or a memory leak); this is unconfirmed.
